questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use brakes. Downshift instead.

questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down and avoid sudden movements. Use both brakes if you need to slow or stop.

questions.question: At night, what is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep at least three seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. You need extra time to notice if it stops and to brake safely.

questions.question: What can increase fatigue when riding?

options.text: Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day. Stop for a break every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as fatigue can hit hard when they wear off.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve toward the area with fewer hazards.
Keep the brake on and try to accelerate.

questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. On a good surface, you can keep the rear brake locked until you stop.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes with road and traffic conditions. Move around the lane to stay safe and help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Which of these is not a cause of motorcycle wobble?
questions.explanation: Wobbles usually come from improper loading, unsuitable accessories, or wrong tire pressure. Do not speed up to escape a wobble.

questions.question: When do you not need to increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see through the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. You need extra space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the rear of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders in back watch them and help if needed.

questions.question: What kind of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: What is the best riding formation for a group?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to single-file when turning, riding curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle makes it hard to control the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops instead of or along with turn signals. When a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and points upward, it means the rider will turn right or move to the right lane.

questions.question: When entering a highway or riding through a curve, how should a group of motorcyclists ride?

options.text: Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation works best most of the time. But switch to single-file when turning, riding through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Use the headlights of the vehicle in front of you to see ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of the vehicle in front of you to see ahead.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: Which action helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Avoid the center lane and follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more slippery.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older is legally intoxicated at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______.
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and unsafe to ride a motorcycle while intoxicated.

questions.question: If you need to brake while riding through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
Brake as hard as you would on a straightaway.
Wait until you are not in the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more gradually than you would on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Try to straighten the motorcycle before braking. If you must brake in a curve, apply the brakes smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, how should it be positioned?

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it better.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips under five miles long at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing down if someone is following too closely. The other driver may not notice the hazard causing you to slow. Also flash your lights if you are slowing in a place where other drivers do not expect it.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders ride in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the lead rider. More experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies partial rear braking when the front brake is applied.
Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
Applies equal braking to both front and rear brakes when either is applied.
Learns and remembers the braking force the rider uses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies partial front braking when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Which type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Speed limit and other regulatory signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for communication when riding in groups. This signal means "follow me."
